title: Bechet and Louis Armstrong; the missed Town Hall concert
summary: Bechet had strained relations with Armstrong; he fell ill on the subway and missed the 1947 Town Hall reunion concert.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: well it's funny down here too at the time they had that Esquire concert about 1945 I guess in January of 45 went all over the country they had some rehearsals here I know they had a couple of local bands I think Sharky's band maybe George Lewis or two or three other local bands here played and they told that when Louis Armstrong was leader of this all-star group had been selected by Esquire partly they had gotten votes there at least Sidney came down to play with him and it ended up in quite a little row I remember they quote Louis saying I'm going to have no two leads in my band
Sidney didn't get along with Louis in the later years yeah I guess not he felt that Louis didn't play the way he did in the old days when they played together
and he was never happy about the 1940 sessions he did with Louis
that Decca session yeah they did
and you remember that Louis Armstrong town hall concert yeah

no Bobby Hackett and Peanuts well you know Sidney was supposed to be on that no I don't remember that in fact the big thing about that concert was Freddie Robbins was a disc jockey who was running a thing and he had every night in the program for a couple of weeks before the concert he talked about this reunion Sidney Boucher and Louis Armstrong that was the big thing about it

and well what happened was Sidney was going on a subway to the concert and got sick and was just lying there practically unconscious and he rode around the subway for hours people thought he was drunk you know and nobody knew where is Sidney I remember being backstage at this thing and Ernie Anderson and Fred Robbins were saying where is Sidney and they wanted me to go on and play and I wouldn't do it because I you'd be upset too naturally well I was upset too and I also felt I wasn't ready for this I wasn't ready to play with Louis Armstrong and Bobby Hackett and everything which I wasn't at that time you know
yeah that's pretty early when was that? forty-seven
forty-seven yeah you haven't played very long then anyway
but I know Sidney had mixed feelings about playing that concert
